**Consequences (testable):**
- On the server tier, interests are chosen only by tap from the catalog, and nothing a parent types leaves the device.
- The interest catalog has no health, religion, ethnicity, or diet entries.

#### FR-68: Linking and consent states

A parent can become the device's linked parent by completing the consent method once (FR-86). Our servers then keep only the linked-parent record. Realizes UJ-10.

**Consequences (testable):**
- State changes follow this table:

  | From \ event | Link or consent | Revoke consent | Unlink | Delete everything | Refund |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Unlinked | Linked (server tier: linked with consent) | — | — | Family's on-device data deleted; model files stay (FR-71) | Basic mode |
  | Linked (on-device tier) | — | — | Unlinked; loosened limits return to defaults | Unlinked; family's on-device data deleted, model files stay; record deletion requested, shown as not yet accepted or accepted, never as completed (FR-71) | Basic mode; still linked |
  | Linked with consent (server tier) | — | Linked without consent; server talk stops | Unlinked; server talk stops; loosened limits return to defaults | Unlinked; family's on-device data deleted, model files stay; record deletion requested, shown as not yet accepted or accepted, never as completed (FR-71) | Basic mode; server talk stops; still linked |
  | Linked without consent (server tier) | Linked with consent (no new purchase) | — | Unlinked; loosened limits return to defaults | Unlinked; family's on-device data deleted, model files stay; record deletion requested, shown as not yet accepted or accepted, never as completed (FR-71) | Basic mode; still linked |

- "Stops" means before the next voice turn and within 60 s, except after a refund, when server talk stops within 24 hours (FR-83).
- On the on-device tier, the linking notice says that no child data is collected.
- A web unlink or record deletion reaches the device at its next successful link check; while online, checks occur at least every 30 days. Offline delivery has no 30-day guarantee. A web record deletion unlinks the device; it does not remotely erase the child's pet.
- "Loosened limits return to defaults" means every setting in FR-69's "Go beyond the SB 1119 defaults" row returns to its default; settings within the defaults are kept.

#### FR-69: Changing limits

One matrix sets who can change which limit. Realizes UJ-11.

| Change | Who |
|---|---|
| Tighten: shorter caps, earlier bedtime, later wake time, avoided words, adding a food rule, Pause | Any parent past the gate |
| Relax within the parent's own settings: a later bedtime or earlier wake time, a longer visit or daily cap up to the SB 1119 defaults, waking Pip after bedtime, removing a food rule, lifting a Pause | Any parent, with the PIN |
| Go beyond the SB 1119 defaults: a visit cap above 1 hour (up to 120 minutes) or a daily cap above 2 hours (up to 4 hours) `[ASSUMPTION: ranges]`, and allowing silly words | A linked parent, with the PIN |

**Consequences (testable):**
- Every change beyond the defaults sends the linked parent an email confirming it (FR-75).
- Pause puts Pip to sleep until a parent lifts it; the child sees a sleeping Pip.
- Settings are stored on the device; the server stores none, except the change-type code needed for FR-69.1 `[ASSUMPTION: CQ-34]`.

#### FR-70: Report a line

A parent can send a flagged line (FR-58) to us as a report, with an optional note, in two taps. Realizes UJ-10.

**Consequences (testable):**
- The parent previews exactly what will be sent: Pip's line as text with names as placeholders, the tier, the app version, and the note (at most 280 characters, with a warning not to include personal details). No child, device, or parent identifier is sent, only a per-submission ID that tells apart retries (§6.2), and our network edge drops the IP address.
- Only named reviewers see reports. Each report is triaged within 2 business days, and a confirmed harmful line leads to a list update and a new evaluation probe.

FR-68 ("Linking and consent states") says a parent becomes the device's linked parent by completing the consent method once (FR-86). After that, our servers keep only the linked-parent record. It realizes UJ-10.

The state table has four rows: Unlinked, Linked (on-device tier), Linked with consent (server tier), and Linked without consent (server tier). Its columns are the events Link or consent, Revoke consent, Unlink, Delete everything, and Refund.

- **Revoke consent:** only the "Linked with consent" row responds. It becomes "Linked without consent" and server talk stops.
- **Unlink:** from any linked state, the device becomes unlinked and loosened limits return to defaults.
- **Delete everything:** on-device family data is deleted and model files stay. For linked states, record deletion is "requested, shown as not yet accepted or accepted, never as completed".
- **Refund:** the result is Basic mode. Server talk stops, and the device stays linked. The table's Unlinked row also shows Basic mode.

The rules under the table cover timing and scope:
- "Stops" means before the next voice turn and within 60 s. After a refund, server talk stops within 24 hours (FR-83).
- Web unlink or record deletion reaches the device at its next successful link check. Checks occur at least every 30 days while online, with no guarantee offline.
- A web record deletion unlinks the device but doesn't remotely erase the child's pet.
- "Loosened limits return to defaults" means every setting in FR-69's "Go beyond the SB 1119 defaults" row. Settings within the defaults are kept.
- On the on-device tier, the linking notice says no child data is collected.
